content:
The image is a close-up microscopic view of plant tissue showing:

- Dense, branching conidiophores with individual conidia (spores) at the tips
- The sporulation is gray-brown in color with a velvety/fuzzy texture
- A dark black mass visible in the upper right (consistent with sclerotia)
- The overall appearance shows numerous stalked spore clusters characteristic of Botrytis cinerea

This matches Gray_Mold precisely: "dense velvety gray-brown spore mass," "spores are light brown-gray on black stalks," and the presence of dark sclerotia. The microscopic morphology — branching conidiophores with clusters of rounded conidia — is the textbook appearance of Botrytis. The coloration is clearly gray-brown, ruling out Late Blight (white fuzzy) or Powdery Mildew (white powdery).
